blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: The wrapper implementations establish no direct holder freeze, while upstream yzUSD and reserve-asset access exposure remains inherited.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-verified 2026-08-09 on both deployments. At Plasma block 29369955 the syzUSD proxy 0xc8a8df9b210243c55d31c73090f06787ad0a1bf6 resolves EIP-1967 implementation 0xa3982582016375a0b25cb7d572379d3d49e5e9c8 and admin 0x7392751a860a51694231c7a0b4a9c853f8169cf0, asset() returns yzUSD 0x6695c0f8706c5ace3bdf8995073179cca47926dc, paused() is false, and freeze-family probes such as isBlacklisted(address) revert; that ProxyAdmin's owner() is Safe 0xa2a9700407934e913c840556b3d29f19cf6f203d with getThreshold() 4 and no timelock. At Monad block 94595184 the proxy 0x484be0540ad49f351eaa04eeb35df0f937d4e73f resolves implementation 0xe536b80e7f859e72ad095d769da1da45b7312d53 and admin 0x7040b88de8a8e63b9dffe2250f8062dcc1ca7331, whose owner() is TimelockController 0xd32ab76a165f1a716986ba8c58344e3df4397f5e with getMinDelay() 43200 seconds. The issuer's pinned source documents pause() as scoped to mint and redeem, adds no transfer hook, and blocks rescueTokens on the vault asset while supply is nonzero, so no live holder-selective freeze exists locally; the live proxy admins mean one could be added by upgrade. Backing is the single 100% reserve slice yzusd-yuzu, whose own verdict is possible over issuer-freezable reserve assets, so the named upstream exposure is retained and the verdict stays inherited rather than being collapsed into a token-local possible.

oracleRisk.summary: syzUSD is Yuzu's staking wrapper over yzUSD; its share price accrues strategy yield and the wrapper does not expose a separate borrower collateral market or token-level liquidation oracle.

branchApplicability.reviewer: OpenAI Codex W1b oracle applicability review
branchApplicability.rationale: Yuzu's syzUSD wrapper uses a share price/exchange rate to convert yzUSD into syzUSD shares and back as strategy yield accrues. That wrapper-local rate is a price-sensitive top-level redemption authority; syzUSD has no borrower-owned debt or separate liquidation branches, while underlying yzUSD remains a dependency.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Plasma is the only reviewed native syzUSD issuance route. Its CCIP LockReleaseTokenPool is cross-chain escrow and remains Bridge Risk rather than native Mint Authority. Ethereum, Monad, HyperEVM, Sei, Pharos, and Berachain are bridge representations with active Chainlink CCIP burn/mint routes: Ethereum, Monad, HyperEVM, Sei, and Pharos run BurnMintTokenPool 1.6.1 pools that are the local token's verified CCIP minter and burner, with the Yuzu owner controlling pool administration and rate limits; Berachain runs BurnMintTokenPool 1.5.1 over a FactoryBurnMintERC20 1.6.2 whose sole minter and burner is the pool, with the Yuzu EOA as token owner and CCIP admin. The canonical Plasma pool now carries six supported CCIP lanes, each mapping back to the canonical Plasma token. The dual-surface BridgeableTokenUpgradeable deployments on HyperEVM, Sei, and Pharos also expose LayerZero OFT machinery, but LayerZero peers read zero on HyperEVM and Sei, and Pharos holds only a one-sided peer to the issuer's Plasma contract 0x0cddd7515586550f16dec1732e0386109e1859e8 whose own peer mapping is empty, so LayerZero remains an exposed surface rather than a live rail; Bridge upgrade/admin and pool controls are explicitly scored here, with an external-validated-network tier.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: OpenAI Codex syzUSD bridge-boundary canonicality verification; extended 2026-09-05 by Claude YuzuRailsCloseout (HyperEVM/Sei/Pharos/Berachain live RPC rail verification)

At the 2026-08-17 and 2026-09-05 observations, each pool was the live token's CCIP minter and burner holder, with Yuzu-owned router, remote-pool, and rate-limit configuration verified; LayerZero peers read zero everywhere except a one-sided Pharos-to-Plasma peer whose Plasma-side counterparty holds no peers.

routes.protocol: Yuzu syzUSD BridgeableTokenUpgradeable representation (Chainlink CCIP CCT with unwired LayerZero OFT surfaces)
routes.reviewNote: At HyperEVM block 45076319 on 2026-09-05, the syzUSD proxy resolves to implementation 0xf8dd5939a0d31c96f1a7f5c0799a5c5d15af7c94, the dual-surface BridgeableTokenUpgradeable contract whose 15,693-byte bytecode carries both LayerZero OFT functions (lzReceive, setPeer, peers, enforcedOptions, endpoint) and OpenZeppelin grantRole machinery; HyperEVMScan shows public tag 'Yuzu: syzUSD Token', historical Set Peer transactions at blocks 33049961 and 39366601, and CCIP role grants at blocks 38838026 and 38838074 by owner 0x4ea00dc0c2b3933b9b41c6cc372832fe844a89ae. Live peers(uint32) reads across EIDs 30100-30400 (including Plasma 30383, Ethereum 30101, Monad 30390) all return zero, so the LayerZero surface is exposed but carries no live peers today; the issuer's current documented transport is Chainlink CCIP, whose security-infrastructure page lists the syzUSD Token Manager lanes 'Plasma <> Monad / Ethereum / HyperEVM / Sei / Pharos' while the LayerZero page documents a Plasma-HyperEVM DVN configuration only. On the CCIP side, TokenAdminRegistry 0xce44363496abc3a9e53b3f404a740f992d977bdf maps this token to BurnMintTokenPool 0xd32ab76a165f1a716986ba8c58344e3df4397f5e (typeAndVersion 1.6.1) whose getToken() returns this token, getRouter() returns 0x13b3332b66389b1467ca6ebd6fa79775ccef65ec matching the Chainlink CCIP HyperEVM directory, owner() and getRateLimitAdmin() return the Yuzu EOA, getSupportedChains() returns only the Plasma selector 9335212494177455608, getRemoteToken(Plasma) returns canonical syzUSD 0xc8a8df9b210243c55d31c73090f06787ad0a1bf6, and inbound (capacity 3,300,000 syzUSD, refill 38.19444 syzUSD/s) and outbound (capacity 3,000,000 syzUSD, refill 34.72222 syzUSD/s) rate limits are enabled. The pool holds both CCIP_MINTER_ROLE and CCIP_BURNER_ROLE on the token and the token's default admin role is held by the Yuzu EOA; total supply read 0.21 syzUSD. This is a CCIP burn/mint representation, not a native issuance deployment, and the LayerZero OFT surface is recorded as machinery only, not a verified live rail.

routes.protocol: Yuzu syzUSD FactoryBurnMintERC20 representation with Chainlink CCIP
routes.reviewNote: At Berachain block 25789509 on 2026-09-05, this syzUSD deployment is a direct non-proxy contract (8,899-byte runtime code, zero EIP-1967 implementation and admin storage) whose typeAndVersion() returns 'FactoryBurnMintERC20 1.6.2'; a bytecode dispatch scan resolved the Chainlink BurnMintERC677 function surface (grantMintRole/grantBurnRole/grantMintAndBurnRoles, getMinters, getBurners, isMinter, isBurner, getCCIPAdmin, mint, burn, burnFrom, maxSupply) with no LayerZero selectors present. getMinters() and getBurners() each return exactly the CCIP pool 0xe8a5517adedaebe99eb27633b95d412f81e5cff7, isMinter(pool) and isBurner(pool) both return true, getCCIPAdmin() and owner() return the Yuzu EOA 0x4ea00dc0c2b3933b9b41c6cc372832fe844a89ae, and total supply read 129,781.69 syzUSD at 18 decimals, so the lane carries live supply. TokenAdminRegistry 0x0944c3fb1db7d165336569221995b31cbe6c8a55 maps the token to this BurnMintTokenPool 1.5.1 whose getToken() returns the token, getRouter() returns 0x71a275704c283486fba26dad3dd0db78804426ef matching the Chainlink CCIP Berachain directory, owner() returns the Yuzu EOA while getRateLimitAdmin() returns the zero address (1.5.1 pool; rate-limit administration unset, owner retains reconfiguration), getSupportedChains() returns only the Plasma selector 9335212494177455608, getRemoteToken(Plasma) returns canonical syzUSD 0xc8a8df9b210243c55d31c73090f06787ad0a1bf6, and inbound (capacity 3,300,000 syzUSD, refill 38.19444 syzUSD/s) and outbound (capacity 3,000,000 syzUSD, refill 34.72222 syzUSD/s) rate limits are enabled. The issuer key-addresses page lists this token on Berachain chainID 80094, while the CCIP page's Token Manager lane list stops at Pharos; the on-chain TokenAdminRegistry registration, the canonical Plasma LockReleaseTokenPool's supportedChains() now including the Berachain selector 1294465214383781161 with getRemoteToken() mapping to this address, and the live bridged supply establish the CCIP rail regardless of that documentation lag. This is a CCIP burn/mint representation, not a native issuance deployment.
